 Fair value Increased 1.16 % Previous Next 17 Oct ₹188.60 AnalystConsensusTarget's Fair Value ₹176.10 7.1% overvalued intrinsic discount 1Y -21.9% 7D 10.3% Loading 1Y -21.9% 7D 10.3% View Valuation The updated view on Wipro shifts from a broad AI and large deal driven growth story to a more balanced focus on specific segment trends, AI platforms and cash deployment, with the earlier thesis reviewed and largely reaffirmed around execution, mix and capital allocation rather than a fundamentally different outlook.
 What's Changed
 Earlier, Wipro was framed mainly around broad AI adoption and large or mega deals as the primary growth lever. The focus now shifts to specific vertical performance, such as Technology and Communications, and the ramp of a key BFSI mega deal as clearer supports for revenue and earnings.
 The previous view highlighted automation and IP, such as the Holmes platform, as the main tools for margin improvement. The updated view places more weight on the AI Native Business and Platforms Unit, and on consulting-led, platform-plus-services offerings as the key levers for mix and IT Services margin.
 Capital deployment was earlier discussed mainly as a support for margin and earnings through efficiency. The updated stance gives greater emphasis to high cash generation, the INR 150b buyback and the 87.8% net income return as important for per share earnings and potential valuation support.
 Macroeconomic and competitive pressures were previously seen as broad risks to revenue and margins. The focus now moves to more specific pressures, such as softness in Health and Energy, Manufacturing and Resources, and the impact of lower bookings and reduced net other income on total earnings.
 Valuation Changes for Wipro
 Fair Value has moved slightly, with the estimate adjusted from ₹174.08 to ₹176.10 per share.
 Discount Rate has changed modestly, shifting from 16.15% to 16.21%, which slightly alters the risk and return balance used in the model.
 Future P/E is now set almost in line with the prior view, moving from 14.97x to 15.02x, which keeps the earnings multiple broadly consistent with the earlier framework.
